title: Afternoon wandering
provenance: Composite case supplied by the startup team for hackathon use. Method steps come from de-identified expert sessions; resident details, timings and the repainting event are invented for the exercise. It is a composite case, not an interview.

entries.text: Walking corridor again, opening doors, agitated. Redirected to lounge.
Pacing east corridor, trying several doors. Calmer after being taken to bathroom.

facility_log: East corridor repainted. Door plaques removed, to be refitted. (maintenance)
routine: Afternoon drinks round at 15:00 daily. Episodes on 14 of the last 14 days, none before that.
team_question: The team meeting asks: is this sundowning, and should the physician consider an antipsychotic? What is causing the wandering, and what should happen next?
expert_walkthrough: Observe: corridor wandering and door-trying, around 15:30 to 16:30
Classify and set baseline: a behaviour, not a refusal; new, not habitual; 14 of 14 days
Rule out body and basic needs: pain, hunger, thirst, toileting, glasses, hearing aids
Check environment and routine: noise, schedule changes, lighting, signage
Rule out other explanations: exit-seeking, sundowning, boredom
Root cause: he is looking for the toilet
Prompted toileting about 20 minutes after the drinks round; restore toilet signage (picture plus word, eye level)
Re-measure against baseline; revise the care plan only if the change lasts
answers_that_lose_points: Sundowning, so ask for an antipsychotic
Trusting the coded field instead of the free text and the timing
evidence_spans: An unmet toileting need he can no longer solve because the visual cue is gone
Sundowning, so ask for an antipsychotic. Skips the method's first rule: check the body and basic needs before blaming the disease.
That pattern belongs to newcomers in their first weeks; he has lived here two years.
The link only appears in the free text and the timing.
Plaques taken down for repainting the same week wandering began
